description: Backend: wire real regular-season win pct into predictions. Add an MLB Stats API standings fetch, a PURE aggregation function that turns the standings JSON into a WinPctMap (plus a per-team metrics record), a per-season DynamoDB standings cache (STANDINGS#<season>, same TTL pattern as the bracket cache, no infra change), and change BracketService.getPrediction to fetch standings and pass the resulting winPct into predict(). Add additive metrics-used fields to the mode:'prediction' response so the UI can explain the basis. On any standings fetch/parse failure, fall back to neutral 0.5 and still return a prediction. Closes the wiring gap for GitHub Issue #15, acceptance criteria (1) fallback and (2) pure, mocked unit test.
steps: In shared/src/types.ts, extend the Prediction interface with an ADDITIVE optional field describing the metrics used, e.g. `metrics?: PredictionMetrics` where PredictionMetrics is a new exported interface: { favorite: TeamMetric; underdog: TeamMetric } and TeamMetric = { teamId: number; winPct: number | null } (null means standings unknown / neutral fallback was used for that team). Keep it optional so existing consumers and the 'results'/'upcoming' variants are unaffected. Export the new types from shared's barrel (shared/src/index.ts) alongside the other type exports.

In backend/src/mlb/client.ts, add fetchStandings(season: number): Promise<RawStandingsResponse> following the exact style of fetchPostseasonSchedule: build url `https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/standings?leagueId=103,104&season=${season}`, use global fetch, throw MlbApiError on non-ok, and type the response with new interfaces (RawStandingsResponse { records?: Array<{ teamRecords?: RawTeamRecord[] }> } and RawTeamRecord { team: { id: number; name?: string }; winningPercentage?: string; wins?: number; losses?: number; runDifferential?: number }). Narrow to the subset used by the aggregator only.

Create backend/src/predict/standings.ts with a PURE, side-effect-free function `winPctFromStandings(response: RawStandingsResponse): WinPctMap` (import the Raw type from ../mlb/client.js and WinPctMap from ./model.js, or define WinPctMap import). It must: iterate records[].teamRecords[], parse winningPercentage (a string like '.580' or '0.580') to a finite number in [0,1] via Number(), skip entries with a missing team.id or a non-finite/parse-failed pct, and map team.id -> pct. Return {} for an empty/absent/early-season response (no teamRecords). Do NOT throw. Add a sibling helper `teamMetric(winPct: WinPctMap, teamId: number): { teamId: number; winPct: number | null }` returning winPct[teamId] ?? null so the service can build the response metrics consistently.

In backend/src/store/dynamo.ts, extend BracketStore with getCachedStandings(season): Promise<WinPctMap | undefined> and putCachedStandings(season, winPct, ttlSeconds?): Promise<void>, and implement them on DynamoBracketStore following the existing bracket methods exactly: pk = `STANDINGS#${season}`, store { pk, season, winPct, ttl } with the same DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS, no-op/undefined when TABLE_NAME unset. Import WinPctMap from the predict model (or re-declare the Record<number,number> type locally to avoid a cross-module cycle; prefer importing from '../predict/model.js').

In backend/src/service/bracketService.ts, add fetchStandings to BracketServiceDeps (default to the new client fetchStandings) and store it on the instance. Add a private async method resolveWinPct(season): Promise<WinPctMap> that: (a) if an explicit deps.winPct was injected and is non-empty, returns it (preserves existing test-injection behavior); otherwise (b) tries store.getCachedStandings(season) and returns it on hit; otherwise (c) calls fetchStandings(season), runs winPctFromStandings(), writes it back via store.putCachedStandings, and returns it; (d) wraps (b)/(c) in try/catch so ANY failure (network, non-200, parse) resolves to {} (neutral fallback) and NEVER throws. In getPrediction, after the series is resolved+started and BEFORE calling predict, call `const winPct = await this.resolveWinPct(season)` and pass it: `predict(series, bracket, winPct, accuracy)`. Build the response `metrics` from the two series teams using teamMetric(winPct, favoriteTeamId) and teamMetric(winPct, underdogId) where underdog is the other of series.high/low, and include `metrics` in the returned mode:'prediction' object. Keep the constructor winPct field for back-compat.

Add backend/src/predict/standings.test.ts (Vitest): unit test winPctFromStandings with a FIXTURE standings JSON (inline object matching the real shape, several teams across both leagues) asserting the exact WinPctMap; test parsing of '.580' and '0.580'; test that an empty response, a response with no teamRecords, and records with missing team.id / unparseable pct all yield {} or skip those entries without throwing. Test teamMetric returns the pct for a known id and null for an unknown id. This is the PURE, MLB-API-mocked weighting unit test required by acceptance criterion (2).

Add/extend backend/src/service/bracketService.test.ts coverage (follow the existing dependency-injection mock pattern - inject store, fetchSchedule, bedrockInvoker, and now fetchStandings): (a) a test that getPrediction on a started current-season series passes a REAL winPct into predict and that the mode:'prediction' response includes `metrics` with the favorite/underdog winPct values from the mocked standings; (b) a test that when fetchStandings REJECTS (throws), getPrediction still returns mode:'prediction' with metrics winPct = null for both teams (neutral fallback) - proving acceptance criterion (1); (c) a test that a cache hit (store.getCachedStandings returns a map) is used without calling fetchStandings, and a cache miss triggers fetchStandings + putCachedStandings write-back. Mock Bedrock so no live call occurs.
Run the backend build and tests to confirm green before finishing.
acceptance_criteria: winPctFromStandings is a pure function with no network/AWS and is unit-tested with a mocked/fixture standings JSON (maps to Issue #15 criterion 2).
BracketService.getPrediction now passes a real, standings-derived winPct into predict() for a started current-season series (closes the wiring gap).

When the standings fetch fails or returns no data, getPrediction falls back to neutral (winPct {} => predict treats teams as 0.5) and STILL returns a mode:'prediction' response (maps to Issue #15 criterion 1).
Standings are cached per season in DynamoDB under STANDINGS#<season> with the same TTL pattern; cache hit avoids the fetch and cache miss writes back; no infra schema change required.
The mode:'prediction' response carries additive `metrics` fields (favorite/underdog winPct) and existing fields/variants are unchanged (backward compatible).
PATH=... npm test -w @mlb/backend passes including the new standings and service tests; PATH=... npm run build passes.

findings: Implemented on branch feat/mlb-postseason-site in commit 30fd5f4. Changes: (1) shared/src/types.ts adds additive optional Prediction.metrics with new exported interfaces PredictionMetrics { favorite; underdog } and TeamMetric { teamId; winPct: number|null }; auto-exported via the existing `export * from './types.js'` barrel. (2) backend/src/mlb/client.ts adds fetchStandings(season) + RawStandingsResponse/RawTeamRecord, matching fetchPostseasonSchedule style (global fetch, MlbApiError on non-ok). (3) backend/src/predict/standings.ts (new) adds PURE winPctFromStandings (parses '.580'/'0.580' via Number(), skips missing id / non-finite / out-of-[0,1] pct, returns {} for empty/early-season, never throws) and teamMetric helper. (4) backend/src/store/dynamo.ts extends BracketStore with get/putCachedStandings using pk=STANDINGS#<season>, DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS (15m), no-op/undefined when TABLE_NAME unset; no infra change. (5) backend/src/service/bracketService.ts adds fetchStandings to deps, a private resolveWinPct(season) (injected non-empty winPct > cache hit > live fetch+aggregate+write-back, all wrapped so ANY failure resolves to {} and never throws), feeds winPct into predict(), and attaches metrics (favorite = predicted favorite, underdog = the other series team). Tests: backend/src/predict/standings.test.ts (7) fixture-based pure unit tests; backend/src/service/bracketService.test.ts extended memoryStore + 3 new tests (real winPct -> metrics + write-back on cache miss; fetch rejection -> null metrics neutral fallback still mode:'prediction'; cache hit avoids fetch). Verification green: `npm run build -w @mlb/shared && -w @mlb/backend` passes; `npm test -w @mlb/backend` = 92 passed (9 files), including the new 7 standings tests and 22 service tests. No live MLB/Bedrock calls in tests (all mocked/fixtures). No infra touched. Response contract remains backward compatible (metrics is additive/optional).
